files.purpose: Provider session driver for the GitHub Copilot CLI: spawns `copilot --headless --stdio` per thread, speaks the Copilot SDK JSON-RPC protocol over Content-Length framing, and maps every session.event notification, permission prompt, server request, tool call and account/quota query onto Droppy Code's ProviderEvent/ApprovalRequest/ToolCall model. Also carries the static catalog helpers (models.list, account.getCurrentAuth, account.getQuota) used for model listing, auth status and plan limits, plus Hydra sub-agent wiring.

side_effects: Launches a child process: `copilot --headless --stdio --no-auto-update --log-level error` plus MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments(), via StdioProcess with Content-Length framing
Writes/reads Copilot session state on disk indirectly: sessions are created under Droppy Code's own id and resumed from ~/.copilot/session-state (per header doc)

JSON-RPC requests over stdio: ping, session.create, session.resume, session.send, session.commands.list, session.commands.invoke, session.abort, session.history.compact, session.history.listRewindPoints, session.history.rewind, session.permissions.setMode, session.permissions.handlePendingPermissionRequest, session.mode.set, session.model.switchTo, session.model.setReasoningEffort, models.list, account.getCurrentAuth, account.getQuota, runtime.shutdown
Network indirectly: the CLI reaches GitHub Copilot for model turns, model list, auth and quota (a turn without Copilot access fails with HTTP 403)
TokenLedger.shared.record(spend:) records input+output tokens on every assistant.usage event with spend > 0
stop() fires two detached Tasks: one requests runtime.shutdown then closes, one sleeps `try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3))` then closes as a backstop
listModels/authStatus/readPlanLimits each spawn a throwaway copilot process in FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory and close it via defer
respondPermission spawns a detached Task per permission answer
loadCommands() spawns a detached weak-self Task to fetch and publish the command list
platform_assumptions: macOS/Unix child process launched from a URL executable with a POSIX working directory (configuration.workingDirectory.path)
Swift Regex literals (#/.../#) with firstMatch(of:) and typed match.output tuples
FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory used as the cwd for catalog-only connections
ISO8601DateFormatter with .withFullDate fallback for quota reset dates
String.hashValue used as the dedupe key for reasoning text (per-process randomized seed, fine because it is session-scoped only)
Depends on the `copilot` CLI being installed and reachable; the SDK protocol version 3 is what was verified (copilot 1.0.83)
A `powershell` tool name is recognized in toolCall mapping, so the CLI itself may report Windows shells, but the host process model is Unix
persisted_fields: sessionId: String - Droppy-generated `UUID().uuidString.lowercased()` unless configuration.resumeID exists; persisted by the CLI in ~/.copilot/session-state and reused on resume

Session-create JSON fields: sessionId, clientName, workingDirectory, streaming(true), requestPermission(true), requestUserInput(true), requestExitPlanMode(true), includeSubAgentStreamingEvents(Bool), isExperimentalMode(Bool), model(String), reasoningEffort(String), customAgents(array), systemMessage{mode:"append", content:String}

Quota snapshot keys read: quotaSnapshots.premium_interactions, quotaSnapshots.chat, quotaSnapshots.completions; sub-fields isUnlimitedEntitlement, entitlementRequests, remainingPercentage, usedRequests, resetDate
Auth fields read: authInfo.login, authInfo.copilotUser.access_type_sku, authInfo.copilotUser.copilot_plan
PlanLimits.Window ids are the literal quota keys: "premium_interactions", "chat", "completions"
Pending-request keys in memory: permission uses the CLI's requestId verbatim, questions use "question-<id.key>", plan exits use "plan-<id.key>"
ui_elements: Approval options for a permission prompt: id "allow" title "Approve" role .approve; id "always" title "Approve for session" role .approveAlways (only when sessionApproval(for:) is non-nil); id "deny" title "Decline" role .decline

Plan-exit approval: title "Implement this plan", kind .plan, options "Implement plan" (id allow, .approve) and "Keep planning" (id deny, .decline); the plan markdown is emitted first as .planCompleted

Shell permission row: title = ToolTitles.unwrapShell(request.fullCommandText) or "Command"; detail joins a non-cwd working directory and the sandbox-bypass reason with " \u00b7 "; sandbox fallback text "Runs outside the sandbox."
Write permission row: kind .fileChange, title = path relative to cwd (resolvedPath ?? fileName ?? "file")
Read permission row: kind .permissions, title "Read <relative path>" (resolvedPath ?? path ?? "file")
URL permission row: kind .permissions, title "Fetch <url>" (url ?? "a URL"), detail "Redirected from <redirectedFrom>"
MCP permission row: kind .tool, title "<serverName> \u00b7 <toolTitle|toolName|tool>", detail = compact args unless the string is "null"
Memory permission row: kind .tool, title "Remember: <fact>" with fact fallback "something about this project"
custom-tool row: kind .tool, title = toolName ?? "Tool", detail = toolDescription
hook row: kind .tool, title = hookMessage ?? toolName ?? "Tool", detail = the tool name only when hookMessage exists
extension-management row: kind .tool, title "<operation.capitalized> <extensionName>" with fallbacks "manage" and "an extension"
Unknown permission kind: kind .tool, title = humanize(kind) with fallback kind "action"

Question surface: a single QuestionRequest.Question with id "answer", header "" (empty), prompt = params.question, choices from params.choices, allowsMultiple false, allowsOther = params.allowFreeform ?? true, isSecret false
Notices: "Context compacted." (info) on successful compaction; "/<name> opens a dialog that only Copilot's own terminal UI can show." (warning) for unsupported command kinds
Command output message id "command-<UUID>"; non-markdown command text is wrapped in a triple-backtick fence as "```\n<text>\n```"

Tool titles fallbacks: "Shell command", "Read file", "Create file", "Edit file", "Search", "Find files", "Fetch page", "Search the web", "Subagent", "SQL query", "Create pull request", "Skill \u00b7 <skill>", "Edit <n> files"
View line-range detail: "from line <start>" when the end is negative, otherwise "lines <start>\u2013<end>" using an EN DASH U+2013

Model list details joined with " \u00b7 ": "<n>\u00d7 premium requests" (integer when the multiplier is whole, else the raw double) and "Enable it in your GitHub Copilot settings first" for policy.state == "unconfigured"
Auth label suffix " \u00b7 no Copilot access" appended to the login (or to "GitHub") when access_type_sku == "no_access"
Plan-limit window titles: "Premium requests", "Chat messages", "Code completions"; plan name rendered as "Copilot <plan>"
feature_notes: start(): connects, then uses configuration.resumeID ?? UUID().uuidString.lowercased() as sessionId and calls "session.create" when resumeID is nil, otherwise "session.resume"; a resume for an id the CLI no longer has fails so the thread starts fresh. After create/resume it always calls applyModes(runtime:interaction:) (a resumed session comes back interactive + manual) and loadCommands(), then returns the id.
Auto mode requires the CLI's experimental flag isExperimentalMode, which is a session-creation setting, so switching into or out of Auto forces the thread to restart the session.

systemMessage is always sent as {mode:"append"} exactly once per session; the content is [hydraPolicy, AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled:)] compactMap'd and joined with "\n\n", so the anti-slop OFF notice still goes out and a resumed thread cannot keep earlier guidance alive.

Hydra native mode sets customAgents = HydraPrompts.copilotAgents(hydra) and includeSubAgentStreamingEvents = true with policy HydraPrompts.policy(for: .copilot, hydra); Hydra heads on another provider instead use HydraPrompts.fallbackPolicy(hydra) and define no CLI agents.

send(): applies modes and model/effort selection first, then beginTurn(); if the text starts with a slash command the CLI knows (commandNames), it calls session.commands.invoke, otherwise session.send. On a throw turnActive is reset to false before rethrowing.
beginTurn() clears shownReasoning and streamedMessages, resets turnError and interruptRequested, and emits .turnStarted(providerTurnID: nil).

Image attachments: only images (Attachment.isImage) are passed, as {"type":"file","path":...,"displayName":...,"mimeType":...} in an "attachments" array; the CLI reads the files itself for vision models.

invokeCommand(): reads result.mode to flip interactionMode ("plan" -> .plan, anything else -> .build) and emits .modeChanged; result.kind "agent-prompt" re-sends result.prompt (or the raw input) as a prompt; "text"/"completed" emits an ANSI-stripped message and finishes the turn; any other kind emits the warning notice and finishes the turn.

ownCommands are intercepted and never registered: allow-all, yolo, permissions, model, models, plan, session, sessions, cwd, cd. Aliases from the CLI list are added to commandNames but only the primary name produces a SlashCommand entry (name + description detail).
interrupt(): only acts while turnActive; sets interruptRequested, cancels every pending request, then session.abort with reason "user_initiated".
compact(): session.history.compact with trigger "manual".

rollback(turns:): lists session.history.listRewindPoints, requires points.count >= turns and takes points[count - turns].eventId, then session.history.rewind with mode "conversation"; failures throw "Copilot has no rewind point for that turn." or result.error / "Copilot could not rewind the conversation." (outcome must equal "success"). File state is not restored here; Droppy Code restores it from its own checkpoints.

resolveApproval(): "allow" -> {kind:"approve-once",approvedInteractively:true}; "always" -> sessionApproval(for:) or the same approve-once; anything else -> {kind:"reject",feedback:"The user declined this action."} and the tool row is marked .declined. Always emits .requestResolved(id:).
Declining a question through resolveApproval answers {answer:"", wasFreeform:true}; answerQuestion joins the first answers value with ", " and sets wasFreeform to !choices.contains(answer).

Plan approval answers {approved:true, selectedAction:"interactive"} and optimistically emits .modeChanged(.build); refusal answers {approved:false, feedback:"The user wants to keep planning. Wait for their feedback before changing anything."}.
stop(): sets isStopping so handleClose does not emit .exited, requests runtime.shutdown (to let the CLI flush its event log) then closes, with a 3 second timer closing as a backstop.

permissionModeName: .supervised and .autoAcceptEdits -> "manual", .auto -> "assisted", .fullAccess -> "allow-all"; session.permissions.setMode is sent with source "rpc" and the reply's mode is trusted (assisted is refused outside experimental mode).
session.mode.set uses "plan" or "interactive".

applySelection(): session.model.switchTo {modelId, reasoningEffort?} only when the model actually changed; a separate session.model.setReasoningEffort when only the effort changed. Local model/effort state is only updated when the request succeeded.

connect(): CLI arguments are exactly --headless --stdio --no-auto-update --log-level error plus MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments(); Settings-connected MCP servers are the only ones the session sees and the user's own are disabled by name for that session without touching their file. The handshake is a `ping` with {"message":"droppy-code"} and a non-nil protocolVersion, else the connection closes and it throws "This `copilot` does not speak the SDK protocol. Update it with `copilot update`."

handleNotification only handles method "session.event"; events for a different sessionId are dropped. With Hydra off, sub-agent events (agentId present) whose type starts with "assistant." or "tool." are dropped except "assistant.usage", so spend still counts; permission prompts always pass. With Hydra on, agent events are wrapped in .agentEvent(agentID:_:).

Event types handled: assistant.turn_start, assistant.message_delta, assistant.message, assistant.reasoning_delta, assistant.reasoning, assistant.usage, session.usage_info, tool.execution_start, tool.execution_partial_result, tool.execution_progress, tool.execution_complete, subagent.started, subagent.completed, subagent.failed, permission.requested, permission.completed, session.mode_changed, session.title_changed, session.error, session.warning, session.compaction_complete, session.idle, session.shutdown. Everything else is ignored.
assistant.turn_start from a head emits .turnStarted(providerTurnID: data.turnId) on the head sink; for the lead it only sets turnActive and emits when a turn was not already active.

assistant.usage spend = inputTokens + outputTokens and is only reported when > 0; TokenSpend carries cachedInputTokens from cacheReadTokens, model from data.model ?? the session model, and agentID for head spend.
session.usage_info -> ContextUsage(usedTokens: currentTokens, windowTokens: tokenLimit).
tool.execution_partial_result maps partialOutput to .toolOutput; tool.execution_progress maps progressMessage to a ToolUpdate(detail:).

subagent.started (Hydra only) emits AgentSpawn with taskID nil, toolUseID = data.toolCallId, description = the stored task brief, else agentDisplayName, else agentName, else "Subagent"; profile via HydraPrompts.profileName(forAgentName: data.agentName). subagent.completed maps cancelled == true to .interrupted otherwise .completed with no summary; subagent.failed maps to .failed with data.error as summary.
session.idle ends the turn: finishTurn(aborted: data.aborted == true). A turn that was interrupted or aborted reports .interrupted, a recorded turnError reports .failed, otherwise .completed.
session.error while a turn is active is stashed in turnError and surfaced at turn end; outside a turn it becomes an .error Notice immediately.
session.mode_changed maps "plan" -> .plan and both "interactive" and "autopilot" -> .build; other values are ignored.
session.shutdown only notices when shutdownType == "error" and errorReason exists.
session.compaction_complete: success true -> info notice "Context compacted."; otherwise the error string becomes a warning notice.

Reasoning dedupe: reasoning shown by assistant.reasoning is hashed (trimmed hashValue) into shownReasoning so a message's own reasoningText copy is not repeated; the message-carried copy is emitted with id "<messageId>-reasoning".

assistant.message emits .messageCompleted even with empty content when that id previously streamed deltas, so an empty final message still closes the row; it then registers every entry of toolRequests as a tool row.

toolRequested is idempotent per call id (guard toolNames[id] == nil). "update_todo" is intercepted and turned into .todos from its markdown checklist instead of a row; "task" stores the brief (description ?? name ?? "Subagent", prompt ?? task) so subagent.started can name the head. A call with non-empty edits immediately gets a follow-up ToolUpdate(edits:).

handleToolResult skips hiddenTools; output prefers error.message on failure, otherwise result.detailedContent ?? result.content; status is .completed, or .declined when the id is in declinedTools, else .failed. success defaults to true when absent.

errorMessage(): default "Copilot reported an error."; text after the marker "GenericFailure, " is parsed as JSON and rewritten as "HTTP <status>: <trimmed body>"; when statusCode == 403, remediation == "sign_in", or the message contains "not authorized to use this Copilot feature" (case-insensitive) it appends " Check that your GitHub account has Copilot access, or sign in again with `copilot login`."

Server requests: userInput.request becomes a QuestionRequest keyed "question-<id.key>"; exitPlanMode.request becomes a plan approval keyed "plan-<id.key>" using planContent (non-empty) ?? summary ?? ""; autoModeSwitch.request is answered {"response":"no"} so a rate limit cannot silently move the user off their chosen model; any other method gets JSON-RPC error -32601 "Droppy Code does not support <method>."

handlePermission ignores requests with resolvedByHook == true. automaticDecision approves everything in .fullAccess, approves kind "write"/"read" in .autoAcceptEdits, approves write/read plus anything the CLI's assistedApproval recommendation == "approve" in .auto, and approves nothing in .supervised; the approve payload is {"kind":"approve-once"} with no approvedInteractively flag.
A "write" permission that carries a non-empty diff updates the tool row with the CLI's own patch (FileEdit with ToolTitles.diffStats additions/deletions) because it beats the row's reconstruction.
When the approval has no reason, promptRequest.assistedApproval.reason (the judge's words) is used instead.

sessionApproval(for:): shell needs canOfferSessionApproval == true and non-empty commands[].identifier -> {kind:"commands", commandIdentifiers:[...]}; write needs canOfferSessionApproval -> {kind:"write"}; read -> {kind:"read"}; url returns {kind:"approve-for-session", domain:<URL host>} directly; mcp -> {kind:"mcp", serverName, toolName(optional)}; custom-tool -> {kind:"custom-tool", toolName}; memory -> {kind:"memory"}; anything else nil. All but the url case are wrapped as {kind:"approve-for-session", approval: ...}.
respondPermission always posts session.permissions.handlePendingPermissionRequest with {sessionId, requestId, result}.

cancelPendingRequests answers permissions with {kind:"cancelled", reason:"The user stopped the turn."}, questions with JSON-RPC error -32800 "The user stopped the turn.", and plan exits with {approved:false, feedback:"The user stopped the turn."}, emitting .requestResolved for each.
handleClose resolves every pending request, clears turnActive, and (unless isStopping) emits .exited with TextCleanup.lastLines(tail).

Tool mapping: MCP calls (server present) become .mcp "<server> \u00b7 <tool>"; bash/powershell -> .command with the command text and the description as detail; read_bash/write_bash/stop_bash/list_bash -> .command humanized with shellId detail; view -> .read with a view_range detail; create/edit -> .edit with a FileEdit built from file_text or old_str/new_str; str_replace_editor dispatches on its command argument (view/create/insert/default); apply_patch parses the envelope's "*** Update File: ", "*** Add File: ", "*** Delete File: " headers into deduped paths; grep/glob -> .search with pattern and joined paths; web_fetch/web_search -> .web; task -> .agent with "<name> \u00b7 <agent_type>" detail; read_agent/write_agent/list_agents -> .agent; skill -> .other "Skill \u00b7 <skill>"; sql -> .other with the query as detail; create_pull_request -> .other; anything else -> .other humanized with a single-line compact-argument detail.
apply_patch reads the patch from the bare argument string, else arguments.input, else arguments.patch; the title is the single relative path when there is one, otherwise "Edit <count> files".

todos(from:) parses a markdown checklist where the marker may be -, *, + or "<digits>."/"<digits>)": "x" (case-insensitive) -> .done, " " or empty -> .pending, anything else inside the brackets -> .active.
humanize() replaces "-" and "_" with spaces and uppercases only the first character.

The header documents that Copilot offers no way to stop a single Hydra head on its own, and that the protocol was verified live against copilot 1.0.83 (protocol version 3): framing, ping, account auth, session create/resume/delete, commands, agent and permission modes, model and effort switching, rewind points, compaction and the event envelope.
unresolved_questions: MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments() is not in this file, so the exact flags it appends (and how user MCP servers are switched off by name) cannot be stated from here.
HydraPrompts.copilotAgents/policy/fallbackPolicy/profileName and AntiSlopPolicy.instructions are external, so the actual system-message and customAgents content is unknown from this file.
JSONRPCConnection's sendsVersion: true behavior (whether it adds a jsonrpc field or a protocol version field) is defined elsewhere; only the call site is visible here.
ProviderRegistry.copilotAuto's id/name/efforts, which is prepended ahead of every listed model, is defined outside this file.
PlanLimitsReader.planName(_:) mapping from the raw copilot_plan string to a display name is external.
The header mentions session delete was verified live, but no session.delete call exists in this file, so where a Copilot session is deleted is not determinable from here.
loadCommands() runs in a detached Task, so whether a slash command typed immediately after start() reliably finds commandNames populated is a race this file does not resolve.
